newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end slightly up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end slightly up but off highs.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended up but were off highs on Wednesday following heavy profit taking in timber firm Barito Pacific and some heavyweights, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index closed up 1.36 points, or 0.20 percent, at 691.34 points after hitting a record high of 695.98 points earlier. However, in broad market sentiment, losers led gainers by 63 to 61, with 58 counters unchanged. Total volume was 331.7 million shares on a turnover of 824.6 billion rupiah.
Brokers and analysts said the index was expected to stay in positive territory on Thursday but the market could see some continued profit taking by speculators.
Timber firm Barito Pacific and conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers dominated overall market activity on speculative interest, brokers said.
Barito Pacific closed 50 rupiah lower at 1,775 rupiah after touching a high of 2,025 rupiah. It was the most actively traded stock, with 34.8 million shares changing hands.

"Approaching the late session, investors, mostly local, started taking profit after a series of rumours, including one that President Suharto's daughter would buy a stake in the firm," a broker said. "The rumour could not be confirmed."
Bakrie closed 25 rupiah higher at 1,200 rupiah on a volume of 24.4 million shares after rising earlier to 1,250 rupiah.

Brokers said the buying was prompted by news PT Nusamba Mineral Industry, a part of the Nusamba Group, wanted to buy a 50.479-percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama Corp in which Bakrie has a 49-percent stake. Indocopper has a 9.36-percent stake in PT Freeport Indonesia, which operates one of the world's largest copper and gold mines in Irian Jaya province.
Profit-taking was also seen in heavyweights such as Telkom and Semen Gresik which pushed down the index. The stocks have a combined weighting of 20.23 percent on the index.
Telkom fell 25 rupiah to 4,175 rupiah on a volume of 4.8 million shares after rising to 4,275 rupiah earlier.
Brokers said the closing price was in line with its closing price of $35-1/4 in New York overnight.
Retailer Matahari, and Multipolar of the Lippo Group were also on the active list ahead of Multipolar's extraordinary shareholders general meeting on Thursday.
The meeting will seek shareholders' approval to take a controlling 50.1 percent stake in Matahari Putra Prima.
Brokers said some selling pressure was seen on both counters in late trading on speculation the meeting would be postponed.
But a Multipolar official denied the speculation.
"Nothing's changed. We will hold the meeting tommorrow as scheduled," the official told Reuters.

Multipolar closed 50 rupiah higher at 2,150 rupiah but was off its intra-day high of 2,250 rupiah, on a volume of 15.1 million shares. Matahari rose 125 rupiah to 2,925 rupiah on a volume of 7.1 million shares.
The strong buying interest in Multipolar boosted sentiment on other Lippo units such as Lippo Securities, Lippo Life, Lippo Karawaci and Lippo Bank, brokers said.
